claims.reason: the page's 'pseudoallergic self-limiting rash' has an exact precoordinated concept: (snomed_concept "Acute urticaria due to pseudoallergy" "disorder") (confirmed with exists; is_a Urticaria = YES). rules.rule: Check for adverse reaction after vaccination
rules.problem: Type (check_for task) and trigger are right. Every checked finding is on the page and in the right column. Minor: the 15/30-minute observation window is not encoded; 'Generally unwell' is checked only to be negated in the pseudoallergic rule (acceptable). No invented items.

Structure mostly follows the page: any2 of system groups OR generalised urticaria OR any single serious sign all lead to the red box 'Treat as anaphylaxis', and probable is justified by that directive. Two deviations: (1) the feeling-faint/unwell group is counted as a body system unconditionally, whereas on the page it only enters the anaphylaxis decision after 'Do symptom/s improve quickly? No'; so light-headedness/sweating that settles on lying down, plus one GI or skin symptom, fires probable anaphylaxis. (2) The page's red box 'Treat as anaphylaxis' has no system_priority_evaluation in this file; it relies on the anaphylaxis page's 'Urgent' evaluation on the active condition, which should be confirmed. Hypotension as a recorded disorder rather than a BP comparison will rarely match.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable pseudoallergic rash after vaccination
rules.problem: 'likely' -> probable is right and the 'isolated rash, not generalised, no other symptoms, remains well' structure is faithful. But (1) the diagnosis concept is the broad 'Non-allergic hypersensitivity reaction'; the exact (snomed_concept "Acute urticaria due to pseudoallergy" "disorder") exists and should be used; (2) the page only calls the rash pseudoallergic after monitoring for at least 30 minutes with no other symptoms, and the rule fires immediately on an isolated rash, dropping that window (e.g. (>= (onset (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Urticaria" "disorder"))) (time_ago 30 minutes)) if minutes are supported). Redundant negations (severe tongue/lip swelling are already excluded by the unqualified tongue/lip swelling negations) are harmless.

summary: The anaphylaxis rule counts feeling-faint/unwell symptoms as a body system without the page's 'symptoms do not improve quickly' gate, so transient vasovagal symptoms plus one other symptom give probable anaphylaxis. The pseudoallergic rule uses the broad 'Non-allergic hypersensitivity reaction' where the exact concept 'Acute urticaria due to pseudoallergy' (disorder) exists, and it drops the page's 30-minute monitoring window before the rash is called pseudoallergic. Every individual finding is genuinely on the page in the right column; nothing is invented, and there is no priority evaluation for the red box in this file.
